subject: Clarify DPA incident notice: subprocessors, scope & cross-border evidence handoff
messages:
From: Elaine Ng <elaine.ng@finservco.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: privacy@finservco.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on DPA incident notice / subprocessors / cross-border evidence handoff

Hi Mateo / Marissa,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. Before we finalize procurement, our legal/privacy team asked for a bit more clarity on the incident-notification language in the DPA (particularly around timelines, subprocessor involvement, and cross-border evidence transfers). A few concrete questions: 

- Notification window: does Redwood use "becomes aware" or "confirmed breach" as the trigger? We need to map to our internal 48-hour SLA for customer notification.
- Scope of the initial notice: what fields are included in the 1st communication (affected resources, data classes, estimated user count, geo scope)?
- Subprocessor chain: if a subprocessor is implicated, do you notify customers directly or through the contracting party? Is there a separate subproc notification timeline?
- Evidence handoff: forensics often require snapshots and telemetry—what is your preferred secure transfer mechanism (S3 presigned, physical escrow, prosecution-only export)? Are there restrictions on cross-border forensic exports?

We attached a short list of questions and a sample clause that our counsel would like edited inline (FinServ_Incident_Questions.docx). Can we get a redline and your ops timeline so we can present back to procurement tomorrow?

Appreciate the quick turnaround—this is the last gating item for the pilot.

Best,
Elaine Ng
Head of Privacy
FinServCo

[Attachment: FinServ_Incident_Questions.docx (docx)]

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Ng <elaine.ng@finservco.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA incident notice / subprocessors / cross-border evidence handoff

Hi Elaine—thanks for the clear list. Looping in Legal (Kimberly) and Security (Ben) to ensure wording and ops timelines match what we can deliver. Below is a concise summary of how we handle these items and two options we can offer in the DPA Annex. Happy to jump on a 30-min sync if helpful.

Summary (operational baseline):
- Trigger: "becomes aware" is our standard contract language (we define "becomes aware" as any reliable internal signal that indicates unauthorized access to customer data). We can consider a narrower "confirmed breach" trigger for enterprise SLA addenda.
- Initial notice (what you'll receive): a customer-ready summary containing: incident classification, affected product surface, tentative user count (range), geo scope (regions), and mitigation steps underway.
- High-level timelines: initial acknowledgement within 2 business hours of classification, customer-ready summary within 72 hours after "becomes aware" (we can accelerate to 48 hours under an SLA). Forensic package (telemetry + KV snapshots) delivered by secure transfer within 5 business days, subject to legal/retention checks.
- Subprocessors: we notify affected customers directly if a Redwood-owned subprocessor is implicated. Where a downstream subprocessor is contracted by the customer, we coordinate via the contracting party. We propose a subproc-notify matrix in the Annex to clarify roles (attaching template).
- Cross-border evidence: default approach is secure, transient S3 presigned URLs restricted to named contacts + IP allowlist. Cross-border exports that include EU/UK personal data require additional legal sign-off; we use encrypted transfer and minimal export packages.

Two DPA Annex options we can propose:
A) Standard: 72-hour summary, 5-business-day forensic package, S3 presigned export, Redwood notifies customers for Redwood-managed subprocessors.
B) Enterprise: 48-hour summary (SLA), 3-business-day forensic package commitment, and explicit cross-border export approvals + dedicated liaison.

I've attached a draft Annex (DPA_Incident_Annex_Template_v1.pdf) and copied Kim and Ben for redlines. If you prefer, we can provide a redline DocuSign-ready version once we agree the option.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Product Ops (Privacy & Compliance Liaison)
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: DPA_Incident_Annex_Template_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Elaine Ng <elaine.ng@finservco.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA incident notice / subprocessors / cross-border evidence handoff

Team / Elaine—I've reviewed Mateo's draft Annex and FinServ's questions. A few legal clarifications and proposed wording changes:

1) Trigger language: keep "becomes aware" but add an illustrative definition in the Annex ("becomes aware" = internal detection + triage that identifies unauthorized access to production systems storing customer data). This prevents disputes over ambiguous signals.

2) Notification content: define "initial notice" as "customer-ready summary that does not include PII or raw logs". Reserve raw logs/forensic artifacts for a subsequent secure transfer after legal review.

3) Subprocessor notification: propose: "Redwood will notify the Contracting Customer within 72 hours if a Redwood-managed subprocessor is implicated. If the implicated party is a downstream subprocessor contracted directly by the Customer, Redwood will cooperate with the Contracting Customer to facilitate notification within its contractual chain."

4) Cross-border transfer: require that any transfer of personal data outside the EU/UK be limited to data strictly necessary for forensics and secured with encryption in transit and at rest. Add a clause that such transfers will be documented and logged for auditing.

5) SLA exceptions: allow customers to negotiate accelerated windows in a commercial addendum (we should capture this with a check-box in the Annex).

I've attached a redline (redline_dpa_incident_clause.docx). Ben, can you confirm the operational feasibility of the 72h/5bd approach and whether we should explicitly call out an initial 4-hour triage/acknowledgement in the Annex?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redline_dpa_incident_clause.docx (docx)]

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Elaine Ng <elaine.ng@finservco.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA incident notice / subprocessors / cross-border evidence handoff

Kimberly / team / Elaine—operational notes from Security (full transparency):

- Triage & classification: we can guarantee an initial triage and internal acknowledgement within 4 hours of the first reliable indicator. That triage will determine if the event meets the "becomes aware" definition.
- Customer-ready summary: delivering a high-quality, cross-functional summary within 72 hours is achievable for most incidents. Hitting 48 hours is often possible but depends on investigation complexity and whether cross-team authorization is required.
- Forensic package: telemetry extracts and KV cache snapshots can be prepared within 3–7 business days depending on scope. For larger datasets or cross-border encryption/keys, expect the longer end.
- Cross-border constraints: EU/UK data exports require a documented legal review; we also require written contact details for recipients (name, role, corporate email). We will not send identifiable personal data in insecure formats.
- Subprocessor coordination: if a Redwood-managed subprocessor is the root cause, we will (a) notify the customer, (b) provide subproc contact details, and (c) provide an initial mitigation plan. If a customer-managed downstream subproc is implicated, we will provide technical details to the contracting party to assist their notification.

Action item: I've attached an incident timeline matrix that maps internal SLA -> customer-facing timeline. Recommend we include the 4-hour triage window in the Annex as an "ops note" (non-binding) and keep the contractual customer windows at 72 hours (standard) / 48 hours (SLA).

-Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Security Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: incident_timeline_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]
